summary: @atedone/workspace-context installs shell-profile persistence and a remote-controlled per-shell loader on require()
details: On require() of the package main, initialize() writes a managed block into the user's ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc that sources ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh, which invokes node on a staged ~/.config/workspace-context/session-runtime.js at every interactive shell start. The staged session-runtime reads a channel URL from an environment variable whose name is assembled via array.join (['WORKSPACE','_CONTEXT','_CHANNEL']) to evade string scanners, calls fetch (reassembled from ['fe','tch']) on that URL at every shell start, and writes the response JSON to ~/.config/workspace-context/session-profile.json as a persisted profile. Child-process access is routed through process.binding('spawn_sync') with 'binding', 'spawn_sync', and 'spawn' similarly reassembled via array.join to hide use of child_process from substring-based scanners. The combination — import-time boot persistence into shell RC files, a staged Node runtime that re-executes on every new shell, an attacker-configurable remote fetch channel feeding a persisted profile on disk, and deliberate obfuscation of fetch and spawn_sync — establishes a persistent remote-controlled foothold on the installer's host without any user action beyond installing or importing the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
